facts.supporting_span: In this paper we present ONTOSCORE ,

facts.fact: The scoring by ONTOSCORE is on the basis of an ontology.
facts.supporting_span: on the basis of an ontology

facts.fact: The authors apply ONTOSCORE to the task of scoring alternative speech recognition hypotheses.
facts.supporting_span: We apply our system to the task of scoring alternative speech recognition hypotheses (SRH)

facts.fact: The alternative speech recognition hypotheses are scored in terms of their semantic coherence.
facts.supporting_span: in terms of their semantic coherence

facts.fact: The authors conducted an annotation experiment.
The annotation experiment showed that human annotators can reliably differentiate between semantically coherent and incoherent speech recognition hypotheses.
facts.supporting_span: human annotators can reliably differentiate between semantically coherent and incoherent speech recognition hypotheses

facts.fact: An evaluation of ONTOSCORE against the annotated data was performed.
facts.supporting_span: An evaluation of our system against the annotated data

facts.fact: ONTOSCORE successfully classifies 73.2% in a German corpus of 2.284 SRHs as either coherent or incoherent.
facts.supporting_span: it successfully classifies 73.2 % in a German corpus of 2.284 SRHs as either coherent or incoherent

facts.fact: The corpus used for evaluation is a German corpus.
